title: Schema-anchoring and deferred-tool-invocation acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define acceptance criteria for a combined feature set: (1) schema anchoring/negotiation when models emit structured frames mid-stream, (2) deferred tool/function invocation semantics (emit-now vs. call-later), and (3) explicit error-mode contracts and resume semantics for partial/streamed responses.
acceptance_criteria: Schema anchoring handshake: every interactive response that intends to emit structured frames MUST include either a top-level schema_anchor object or the first frame MUST be a 'schema_announce' frame. If neither is present, server treats the stream as 'unstructured' and applies best-effort parser rules; this behavior must be documented and tested.

Monotonic checkpoint frames: streamed structured responses MUST include explicit checkpoint frames at least every 2MB or every 10 seconds (whichever comes first). Each checkpoint frame must contain a monotonic checkpoint_id, byte_offset, last_applied_schema_version, and a cryptographic frame_hash. The platform must persist checkpoints for 48 hours to enable resume/reconciliation flows.

Deferred tool invocation contract: model may emit a tool_call frame with "deferred": "true" and a resume_token. On receiving a deferred tool_call the control plane must respond with an immediate 202-equivalent acknowledgement containing tool_call_id and expected max_latency. The actual tool execution can be scheduled asynchronously; the system must provide delivery guarantees (at-least-once) when idempotency_key is provided, or exactly-once when the downstream tool supports idempotency and platform-level deduplication is enabled.

Tool-call idempotency and conflict handling: every tool_call (deferred or immediate) must carry an idempotency_key or the platform will assign a deterministic id. Replayed or resumed tool_calls with the same idempotency_key must not result in duplicate side effects. Conflicts (semantic mismatch for same idempotency_key) must be surfaced as a 409_CONFLICT with original tool_call_id and conflict_reason.

Resume semantics for partial streams: clients may reconnect with a resume_token and request frames after last_checkpoint_id. The server must be able to return any missing frames (or a reconciliation diff) and indicate whether any deferred tool_calls were executed during the gap. Resume is best-effort; server must provide an explicit 'resume_status' in the initial resumed stream header with values: OK_CONTINUE | PARTIAL_REPLAY | FULL_RECOMPUTE.

Error-mode taxonomy and expected handling: define at minimum three classes: TRANSIENT (retryable within backoff window), REPARABLE (needs prompt prompt/PR changes or mapping), and FATAL (client should abort). Platform must map internal failures to stable error codes: X_TOOL_TIMEOUT, X_SCHEMA_VIOLATION, X_CHECKPOINT_LOST, X_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Each emitted error frame must include suggested remediation and a telemetry_id for tracing.

Fallback and graceful degradation: when a tool endpoint is unavailable, the runtime must choose one of the configured policies (FAIL_FAST, FALLBACK_TO_LOCAL_MODEL, RETURN_PARTIAL_WITH_WARNING). Acceptance requires an automated test where tool returns 503 and system demonstrates the selected policy and surfaces a structured warning frame to the client.

Schema evolution rules: adding optional fields is allowed (backwards compatible). Removing or renaming fields requires an explicit schema_migration frame and a negotiated rollout (canary rate and automatic roll-back). Platform must reject incompatible schema changes in production mode unless a migration plan is attached; tests must include a migration with canary=10% that auto-rolls-back on >5% consumer parse failures.

Observability and traceability requirements: every frame (schema_announce, data, checkpoint, tool_call, error) must emit telemetry with fields: trace_id, frame_id, checkpoint_id (if present), model_version, node_id. Dashboards must show per-route counts of deferred tool calls, median tool latency, tool success rate, resume success rate, and checkpoint durability.

E2E test matrix: the feature must have automated tests that cover: immediate tool invocation success, deferred invocation with resume/dedup, mid-stream schema change with checkpoint and resume, tool 503 fallback behavior, idempotency conflict scenario, and long-running streams with multiple checkpoints. Tests must assert no data duplication, correct forward-compat parsing, and correct error-code surface mapping.

Security and compliance: tool payloads classified as sensitive must be encrypted at rest with KMS and marked in the tool_call frame with sensitivity=high. Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) MUST honor customer-managed KMS keys. Include a security_review_required flag set to true and a checklist entry that verifies PII redaction tests for sample tool payloads.

Acceptance thresholds: rollout criteria require (a) deferred-tool success rate >= 99.5% over a 24h synthetic workload, (b) resume_success_rate >= 99% across corner-case tests, (c) schema-violation false-positive rate <= 0.1% when using the recommended schema validator. These metrics must be captured in the release dashboard before GA sign-off.
